All Browser E2E scenarios passed 22/22 (19 carried over from S1-S5 plus 3 new S7 scenarios: editor-group split, PNG binary-fallback placeholder, Markdown plain-text fallback).

E2E-003 completed on 2026-07-31 against the absolute-path debug Plain.app: an exact unsaved edit was backed up to the real Rust store, survived kill -9 and process relaunch as a dirty editor, saved byte-exactly and discarded its backup, then stayed absent after another cold restart. Real FSEvents deletion/restoration toggled the Deleted tab decoration, and a dirty editor plus external rewrite produced exactly Reload/Save As.../Details with no Retry/Overwrite; Reload showed the external bytes. The run found and fixed stale root-capability/version metadata after process restart by single-root authority remapping plus byte-identical SHA-256 baseline rebasing, while external changes still fail closed into the conflict path.
platformGaps: The real Rust WindowEvent::CloseRequested close handshake (veto until the last throttled backup is confirmed flushed, then allow close) is not implemented; PlainWorkingCopyBackupTracker.onFinalBeforeShutdown always returns false, so a normal window close may lose the most recent throttled backup write. E2E-003 safely remaps an expired root capability only when exactly one workspace root is currently authorized. A persisted backup whose old authority is absent in a multi-root workspace remains intentionally unrestored rather than being guessed onto the wrong root; multi-root cross-process backup identity mapping would require storing a stable root identity in the payload.

S2's externally-deleted-open-file DELETED detection uses a bounded per-root LRU (256 entries) of resources seen through plainReadFile as an approximation of "currently open files", not a precise open-editor/working-copy reference count; root revocation does not proactively clear this LRU, it only shrinks lazily as new reads evict old entries (harmless because the revoked root stops receiving wakes), so the approximation can lazily retain entries past root removal.

The two new S5 frontend files (plain-workspace-backup-service.ts, plain-workspace-backup-tracker.ts) reuse and minimally extend existing Harness closed-set checks (MIDDLE_SERVICE_DESCRIPTORS, ALLOWED_MONACO_APP_IMPORTS, isAllowedBridgeIdentifier) rather than adding a dedicated AST hostile-mutation suite of the density used by earlier F020 slices; only the real source passing the existing checks was used as positive evidence.

features.name: Quick Open, workspace search and replace
acceptance: File and content search honor ignore and include/exclude rules
Results stream and cancel without blocking the UI
Replace plan validates file versions before writes

results: pnpm check passed in full on 2026-07-23: 38 frontend test files, 725 cases, 2300 frontend modules, 2134 bundle sources, 203 recorded migration-debt files and Rust 345/345.

All Browser E2E scenarios passed 32/32 (31 carried over from S1-S4 plus 1 new F040 S5 scenario proving the search.exclude default excludes a node_modules directory from both Quick Open file search and Search view text search).
The new S5 scenario additionally passed a focused repeat (--repeat-each=3, --retries=0) before the full-suite run, matching every earlier slice's own acceptance discipline.

Codex completed E2E-004 on 2026-07-31 and then passed pnpm check in full: 81 frontend test files/1694 cases, 1985 bundle sources/53 tracked debt files, and Rust 1178/1178. Focused validation additionally passed the Rust search module 18/18, search/replace unit tests 29/29, the existing replacement Browser matrix 4/4, and the new stale-unopened-file Browser regression 1/1.
nativeScenarios: F040 introduces no changes to the native file open/read/save IPC surface: Quick Open's "open match" and every replace path's per-resource save both route through the exact same native workspace read and versioned-write (wv1/PLR1/PLW1) chain already validated at native desktop level during F020/F030's own acceptance (system folder picker, exact-byte CRUD, versioned save conflict handling). No native-desktop scenario was executed specifically for F040's own additions in this feature -- the bounded Rust file/text-search traversal, gitignore/exclude matching, streaming wake/poll/cancel protocol, and replace coordinator are all new Rust/TypeScript surface with no prior native evidence to inherit.

Codex completed E2E-004 on 2026-07-31 against a 5,008-file real directory tree. A high-frequency query streamed 249 visible results in the first sample; switching it while active to a unique query completed at 1 result in 1 file with no old-result residue. Root and nested .gitignore rules and the default node_modules search.exclude all held in both Search and Quick Open, while an unignored nested sibling remained discoverable. Cmd+P opened the unique target with editor bytes exactly matching disk. A normal replacement produced SHA-256 18cb73e1bfb2d14486e5170419c9c4f5f5eaa566dd5b6ab6fca44e7578030062. A stale unopened-file replacement now fails before any edit or write, offers exactly Reload/Save As.../Details, and leaves external disk bytes unchanged at SHA-256 5c16bbd900c1ebb831e7eb1d066c6511f573ffe762d5434538f61c8cd163b681.

E2E-004 exposed and fixed two native-only defects. TextSearchHandle::close previously joined the producer before dropping a full bounded queue's receiver, deadlocking query replacement; it now disconnects the receiver first. Search matches also previously lacked their expected source text, so an unopened file changed externally could be silently corrupted at stale coordinates; matches now carry expectedText and the coordinator validates every current range before any edit/write, routing mismatches to the existing conflict UI with zero native writes.
platformGaps: Rust's regex engine (the `regex` crate) is linear-time only: no PCRE2, lookaround, or backreference support in search patterns, narrower than upstream's optional PCRE2 mode; an invalid or unsupported pattern surfaces as a Warning message rather than being silently accepted or crashing.

Replace substitutes text literally and does not support `$1`-style capture-group backreferences in the replacement text -- Rust does not return capture groups to the frontend (a deliberate narrowing, stated alongside the regex limitation above, not hidden).

Replacing across multiple files produces one independent undo entry per file rather than one shared cross-file undo group -- a deliberate isolation trade-off (F040 S4) so one file's save failure never blocks or rolls back another file's successful replace.

`search.useIgnoreFiles`/`search.useGlobalIgnoreFiles`/`search.useParentIgnoreFiles` have no registered configuration schema; Rust's search domain hardcodes "always honor .gitignore, never global/parent ignore files" and reads no such flag from any request DTO, so registering a schema for settings neither side consumes was judged actively misleading rather than treated as a completeness gap (F040 S5 decision).

Symlink exclusion from search results is proven by 3 Rust unit tests (F040 S2) and one browser-mock-level unit test (tests/unit/workspace-search-bridge.test.ts, "never reports a symlink as a match and never traverses through one"), not by a live Browser/Playwright scenario -- the shared installNativeIpcMock fixture helper used by every Browser E2E test does not expose symlink-node injection through its extraFiles parameter, and adding that plumbing was judged to risk the ~30 other scenarios sharing it for marginal signal beyond the existing unit-level proof against the identical mock code.

"Replace All in File" (per-file granularity) shares its code path with "Replace" and "Replace All", both of which have dedicated Browser E2E coverage, but it has no dedicated Browser E2E scenario of its own (F040 S4 decision; unit tests and code review cover its shared logic).
An over-8-MiB unopened file's replace failure has no dedicated Browser E2E of its own; the underlying 8 MiB read limit itself is already covered by earlier workspace read slices (F020).

Root-relative search results are not paired with a rootId in the wire response (F040 S2 documented assumption): Plain currently only ever authorizes a single workspace root, so this has not caused an observable issue, but a future multi-root search would need this addressed first.
Windows and Linux native packaging remains F120.
Zeroing the monaco-vscode-api bundle migration debt remains F110.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: File and content search honor ignore and include/exclude rules
acceptanceResults.result: F040 S2's Rust file search honors .gitignore with per-directory layering (deepest layer wins; negation and nested overrides both tested) and applies search.exclude/files.exclude via excludeGlobs, proven end-to-end by the S2 Browser E2E (a .gitignore-ignored sibling file never appears in Quick Open, its non-ignored sibling does and opens on Enter) and by S3 reusing the identical gitignore/exclude plumbing for text search. F040 S5 additionally registered the upstream-matching search.exclude defaults and fixed text search to merge files.exclude/search.exclude like Quick Open. E2E-004 then verified the real Rust semantics on 5,008 disk files: root-ignored, nested-ignored, and node_modules matches were absent from both Search and Quick Open, while the unignored nested sibling was present and Cmd+P opened a unique target with exact disk content. The `filePattern` include remains a Rust-side case-insensitive subsequence prefilter rather than upstream glob syntax; Rust always honors workspace .gitignore and intentionally exposes no unused global/parent ignore setting. Symlink exclusion remains covered at Rust/unit level as documented in platformGaps.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Results stream and cancel without blocking the UI
acceptanceResults.result: F040 S3 implemented the streaming text-search protocol (workspace_search_text_start/poll/cancel: explicit wake plus frontend pull with bounded backpressure) and proved its UI contract in Browser E2E. E2E-004 supplied the missing real-scheduler/real-disk evidence: a high-volume query over 5,008 files rendered 249 results in the first sample, and switching while it was still active completed at a single unique result with no old-result residue. That run exposed a real close-order deadlock when the producer was blocked on a full queue; TextSearchHandle::close now takes and drops the receiver before joining the producer, with a deterministic Rust regression test. File search remains a bounded request-response with a client-side 512-result cap and stale-response discard.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Replace plan validates file versions before writes
acceptanceResults.result: F040 S4's replace coordinator uses the same versioned wv1/PLR1/PLW1 save chain as manual edits, and its open-model conflict behavior remains covered by Browser E2E. E2E-004 first verified a normal real-disk per-match replacement, then demonstrated a missing precondition: an unopened file changed externally after search could be silently modified at stale coordinates before the save token existed. Search matches now carry exact expectedText; before applying any edit or issuing any write, the coordinator resolves the current model and verifies every recorded range. A mismatch leaves the result visibly failed, shows exactly Reload/Save As.../Details, performs zero native writes, and preserved the external file at SHA-256 5c16bbd900c1ebb831e7eb1d066c6511f573ffe762d5434538f61c8cd163b681 in the real desktop rerun. Literal replacement, independent per-file undo, the shared Replace All in File path, and the 8-MiB uncovered edge remain the documented narrowings in platformGaps.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Import local VSIX and unpacked theme directory
acceptanceResults.result: F050 S1 built a bounded, capability-relative VSIX (zip) unpacker (zip crate, enclosed_name/is_symlink entry checks backstopped by Plain's own RelativePath::parse_wire since enclosed_name only catches `../` depth underflow and not absolute-path/drive-letter prefixes -- see the implementation-deviation record) with entry-count/per-entry/aggregate byte caps enforced against actually-read bytes, proven by 17 Rust tests covering zip-slip, symlink entries, oversized entries, oversized packages, zip bombs, corrupt/empty archives and clean round-trips; directory import (S1) shares the identical staging/limit machinery via an explicit non-recursive stack walk, covered by 4 more Rust tests. S2 layered manifest/theme-document validation on top (JSONC with exactly comments+trailing-commas, contributes.themes[] path/uiTheme validation, include-chain cycle/depth/file-count budgets, .tmTheme structural checks) with 19 further error-code tests. S3 exposed both paths as theme_import_vsix/theme_import_directory Tauri commands behind a real native file/directory picker, consumed end-to-end by the frontend (registerExtension/registerFileUrl against the imported package's own resource whitelist) and proven live by Browser E2E. E2E-005 then exercised the VSIX command through the real macOS system picker, verified a legal package plus two representative hostile packages and the exact on-disk state, and completed cross-restart selection/removal persistence. acceptanceResults.acceptance: Apply workbench colors and TextMate token colors
acceptanceResults.result: Plain never registers an extension-point handler at all (the upstream one is structurally unreachable under NullExtensionService, the root cause S0's own probe discovered and fixed): PlainThemeRegistry/PlainThemePicker construct ColorThemeData instances directly from each manifest's contributes.themes[] entry (built-in via getBuiltinExtensions(), imported via the S3 coordinator's local registerExtension/registerFileUrl call) and hand them straight to IWorkbenchThemeService.setColorTheme()'s own instanceof ColorThemeData fallback branch -- proven live by the S0 Browser E2E (`.monaco-workbench` carries real vs-dark/theme classes and a real `--vscode-editor-background` CSS variable instead of the previously-undiscovered unthemed placeholder) and by every subsequent slice's own scenarios reusing the identical apply path for imported themes. Applying colors requires a real IExtensionResourceLoaderService, which no existing override package provided (S0's own PlainExtensionResourceLoaderService closes that gap); token colors flow through the same ColorThemeData#ensureLoaded resource read. `.tmTheme` files are only structurally validated (S2), never parsed into token rules by this Rust domain -- token color application through .tmTheme (a tokenColors string reference) is exercised end-to-end by the S3 whitelist/registerFileUrl path but the actual TextMate scope-to-color resolution is entirely upstream Monaco/TextMate machinery this feature does not modify.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: JSONC, include and tmTheme fixtures pass
acceptanceResults.result: S2's manifest.rs parses package.json and every theme document with jsonc-parser configured for exactly `{allow_comments: true, allow_trailing_commas: true}` and every other option explicitly false (compile-time const-asserted, not just tested) -- deliberately narrower than upstream's looser JSON5-adjacent dialect. include chains are walked with an explicit visited-set (cycle rejection) and a depth cap of 32, plus a whole-package file-count budget of 64 shared across every contributes.themes[] entry's own chain -- both caps independent by design (see the frozen research doc's decision 2). `.tmTheme` files get a structural-only check (`<?xml` header + `<plist` + `<dict` presence) rather than a full plist parse, a deliberate scope line (the bytes are never executed or otherwise consumed by this Rust domain -- the real XML-to-token-rule parsing is Monaco/TextMate's own job downstream of the whitelist read). The frontend's own multi-tab/split lifecycle (TerminalTabsModel, TerminalPaneController) is proven end to end by 4 Browser E2E scenarios: two tabs with independently-alive sessions where closing one leaves the other running, 'Plain: Kill Terminal' closing only the active tab, a split producing two independently-sized-and-sessioned panes, and a reload while multiple tabs (including a split) are open tearing down with zero pageerror. acceptanceResults.acceptance: Backpressure and output fragmentation tests pass
acceptanceResults.result: Byte-level PTY->VT backpressure: flow.rs's own unit tests cover the high/low water mark hysteresis in isolation (stays_clear_below_the_high_water_mark, reaching_the_high_water_mark_pauses_until_the_low_water_mark, wait_until_clear_to_read_blocks_while_paused_and_unblocks_on_ack, cancel_wakes_a_paused_waiter_and_reports_cancelled, an_over_generous_ack_saturates_at_zero_rather_than_underflowing); service/tests.rs's output_well_beyond_the_high_water_mark_still_arrives_completely_and_in_order re-proves the same gate against a real subprocess generating ~112 KiB (2,200 lines) -- well beyond the 100,000-byte high water mark -- while continuously acking as a real frontend would, observes the reader was in fact paused, and asserts the final viewport content is byte-perfect with every frame's sequence number strictly consecutive (no gaps, no reordering, no silent drops). VT->frontend frame-level backpressure: FrameEmitGate's single-outstanding-frame credit is proven in pure unit tests (frame_emit_gate_single_credit_and_tolerant_ack_semantics, frame_emit_gate_does_not_spend_credit_or_a_sequence_number_on_a_clean_snapshot) and against a real session (frame_emission_is_gated_until_the_previous_frame_is_acked: a second frame does not appear until the first is acked, and the coalesced content fed in the meantime is exactly what the freed frame reports). Output fragmentation (this slice's own gap-fill): vt/tests.rs's feeding_an_escape_sequence_split_across_two_reads_parses_identically_regardless_of_the_split_point feeds the same SGR-plus-newline byte stream split into exactly two feed() calls at every one of its 17 possible byte offsets and asserts a byte-for-byte-identical DirtyFrame to a single whole feed() at every one; feeding_the_same_bytes_one_byte_at_a_time_produces_an_identical_dirty_frame_to_one_call repeats this at the worst-case one-byte-per-call granularity; feeding_a_multi_byte_utf8_character_split_across_two_feed_calls_still_decodes_correctly proves a 2-byte UTF-8 character (é) split exactly between its two bytes across two feed() calls still decodes to the complete character rather than mojibake or a dropped cell. A Browser E2E frontend-level complement ('a high-throughput burst of output is coalesced by the single-frame credit gate instead of stalling the UI or dropping content') pushes 500 lines with no yield in between through the same mocked single-credit gate the Rust FrameEmitGate mirrors, and proves the burst's last line still reaches the screen, the number of real terminal_ack round trips stays under 10 regardless of the 500 lines pushed (proving genuine coalescing, not just speed), and the page accepts further keyboard input immediately afterward. WebGL/beamterm upgrade judgment (the deferred decision point docs/research/2026-07-24-libghostty-terminal.md left open): not upgraded. The architecture's own single-frame emission credit already caps the DOM renderer's paint rate at whatever the display's refresh rate allows, independent of how fast the pty itself produces bytes -- a slow consumer only delays the next ack, which throttles frame production upstream rather than ever asking the DOM to paint faster than it can; the renderer additionally groups each row's cells into contiguous same-style <span> runs rather than one element per cell, bounding real DOM node count well below cols x rows. Combined with the real ~112 KiB/2,200-line throughput test and the 500-line Browser burst test above showing no stall and no dropped content under load, there is no real performance deficit driving a WebGL/beamterm upgrade today; DOM MVP is judged sufficient and the upgrade is deferred rather than pursued speculatively.

platformGaps: This feature deliberately ships no credential-entry UI of its own. A missing or incomplete credential fails cleanly and quickly (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 with GIT_ASKPASS pinned to a rejecting program) instead of hanging a child process forever on a TTY that a GUI application does not have. Repositories whose credentials are already resolvable through a configured credential helper or ssh-agent work normally.

fetch/pull/push run the plain, unscoped git command (no remote/refspec arguments); @{upstream} is used only as a precondition check (pull/push refuse before spawning when the current branch has no upstream at all, matching what a bare command would refuse anyway) and by pull's own implicit merge step, not as a guarantee on what fetch/push themselves touch. A plain fetch updates every remote-tracking ref the remote's own configured refspec covers, not only the current branch's upstream (verified empirically against a multi-branch remote); a plain push only happens to touch just the current branch because of today's default push.default=simple, not because this code enforces that scope (verified empirically that push.default=matching uploads every matching local branch instead). There is no UI for choosing a different remote/branch/push.default than the repository's own configuration, or for setting an upstream, consistent with the research document's "never a general-purpose git_run" constraint.

The ahead/behind counts shown in the confirmation preview reflect the last known remote-tracking state and can be stale before a fetch. This is inherent to --force-with-lease semantics rather than a defect.

Hunk-level staging is reachable only through the `Plain: Stage First Change in Active File (Hunk)` command and only for hunk index 0; there is no gutter or diff-editor "Stage Selected Ranges" affordance yet.

The locale-independence acceptance could not be proven the obvious way: this host's Apple Git 2.50.1 is not compiled with gettext (verified via --build-options and by forcing LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8), so asserting that real command output stays English would pass vacuously and prove nothing. It is instead proven structurally -- LANG/LC_ALL are unconditionally overridden for all three GitExecModes even when the test process itself is given hostile LANG/LC_ALL values, with a real subprocess echoing its own $LANG/$LC_ALL back through a hooks fixture to confirm the override reaches the child. A host with a gettext-enabled git would allow the stronger direct assertion.

S5 built and tested an isolated primitive for it (`exec::spawn_adapter_as_tcp_companion`, confirmed via the `Tcp` variant rather than `spawn_adapter`'s hardcoded `Stdio` variant, with bidirectional isolation tests proving a subject confirmed only for one transport variant cannot be borrowed by the other spawn path) but deliberately did not connect it to `DebugSessionService::start_session`'s TCP branch, which still only ever calls `tcp::connect_adapter` (connect-only). Making it production-usable still needs a bounded retry-connect loop (a freshly spawned listener's first connect attempt will typically ECONNREFUSED) and a new configuration-surface field (a `spawnBeforeConnect`-style flag threaded through the frontend config parser and `DebugSessionStartRequest`) -- both judged out of scope for a 'robustness' slice and explicitly left as a documented follow-up in `src-tauri/src/debug/mod.rs`'s module doc, not silently dropped.

runInTerminal was never actually triggered end to end by either of this feature's two real test adapters during development (debugpy defaults to `console:"internalConsole"`, and no launch configuration was constructed that would make lldb-dap request it); its real, spawn-a-real-TerminalService-session implementation and Rust integration test (S4) were both exercised against a synthetic, purpose-built mock adapter that emits a `runInTerminal` reverse request on demand, not against genuine lldb-dap/debugpy behavior. E2E-010 registers a real-adapter-triggered `runInTerminal` scenario to close this gap.

`runInTerminal`'s `kind` field (`integrated`/`external`) is deliberately never inspected -- Plain has exactly one terminal facility (the integrated terminal) and building a second, higher-risk spawn surface to shell out to an OS-native terminal application for a branch that has never been exercised was judged not worth the new attack surface; every `runInTerminal` request is routed through the same integrated-terminal path regardless of what `kind` an adapter declares, proven by a real three-way (`integrated`/`external`/absent) Rust test asserting identical behavior.

The Disassembly view (`supportsDisassembleRequest`, real and present on lldb-dap's own capability set) is explicitly excluded from v1, matching the frozen research document's own scope line; DAP's own in-flight request cancellation is absent because the protocol itself defines no such mechanism, not because of an implementation gap; `Plain: Start Debugging` always uses the first configuration in launch.json with no QuickPick for multiple configurations; the Watch view does not support nested `variablesReference` expansion of a compound evaluate result (only its top-level `result` string is shown); hit-count conditional breakpoints (`hitCondition`) are not implemented, matching the frozen research document's own S3 scope line.

`output_gate`'s discard policy is a per-category oldest-bytes-first budget (`DEBUG_OUTPUT_MERGE_CAP_BYTES` = 1 MiB per category, `DEBUG_OUTPUT_MAX_CATEGORIES` = 16), not a single global memory budget -- worst case, a malicious/malformed adapter that concentrates output into a small number of categories and drives each to its cap can hold up to 16 MiB rather than one bounded global figure; judged acceptable (still a finite bound, and 16 already generously exceeds the ~5 categories the real DAP specification defines) and not tightened further. No test drives a single DAP message to the real 64 MiB `MAX_DAP_MESSAGE_BYTES` boundary itself -- this feature's own real large-object benchmarks (2000-frame stack, 50,000-element array) prove real large-object scenarios sit far below this ceiling, not how the framing layer behaves exactly at or beyond it, which was not required by this slice's own acceptance scope.

Zeroing the monaco-vscode-api bundle migration debt remains F110; Windows and Linux native packaging, and the macOS code-signing entitlement this feature's own research surfaced as a prerequisite for native-debugger acceptance, remain F120.

This feature adds no new @codingame/monaco-vscode-* dependency at all -- the pinned runtime dependency count is unchanged at 17, and the 15 codingame packages in package.json are exactly those F010-F090 already pinned. That is the opposite of F090, which did adopt multi-diff-editor-service-override, and it is not a stylistic preference: the debug-service-override is structurally unusable here rather than merely Chat-coupled. contributes.debuggers and contributes.breakpoints are ExtensionsRegistry extension points, and with no extensions and a NullExtensionService that activates nothing, ConfigurationManager.getDebugger(type) is permanently empty, so the type-resolution path is dead even with Chat and Task stripped out. DebugService additionally constructs AdapterManager and ConfigurationManager directly rather than taking them injected, so neither can be replaced. The debug UI, session state machine, framing and transports are therefore all self-built.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Stdio and TCP transports pass fragmented frame fixtures

S1's own TCP test fragments a real initialize request into 74 3-byte chunks with a 3ms gap between them against a real listening debugpy.adapter and confirms correct reassembly; the S0 stdio fixtures and the S1 TCP fixtures both pass. Real desktop-scale fragmentation against a genuinely slow/adversarial network path is not exercised beyond this and is part of E2E-010's remaining scope.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Breakpoints, stepping, stack, variables and evaluate work
acceptanceResults.result: S3 delivered Monaco glyph-margin breakpoints (three-state verified/unverified/rejected, condition/logMessage editing gated by real Capabilities negotiation, not an assumed-always-on feature), a call-stack ViewPane driving frame selection, and a variables view with real lazy variablesReference expansion plus start/count pagination (proven against a real 5,000-element page in Rust and a real paginated 150-element sequence in Browser E2E) and a Watch view reusing debug_evaluate(context:"watch"). S4 added continue/next/stepIn/stepOut/pause, gated on real session thread state after this feature discovered the task instruction's assumed Capabilities fields (supportsContinue etc.) do not exist in the DAP specification -- see results for the correction. All of it is proven against real spawned Python mock adapter subprocesses in Rust (including a benchmark against 2000 stack frames and a 50,000-element array) and by 11 new Browser E2E scenarios across S3/S4; S3's own mandatory real-DOM-assertion Browser E2E discipline caught and fixed a defect that had made conditional-breakpoint/logpoint editing unreachable since this feature's own first implementation of it (right-click deleted the breakpoint before the edit popup could use it) -- see results for detail. No real native adapter (lldb-dap) has driven any of this end to end on a real desktop; that remains E2E-010.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: runInTerminal uses the integrated terminal
acceptanceResults.result: S4 replaced S2's placeholder (forward-a-diagnostic-event-and-auto-reject) with a real implementation: an AppHandle-free core function (`handle_run_in_terminal_reverse_request`) parses RunInTerminalRequestArguments and calls a new internal `TerminalService::start_program` API (not the `terminal_start` Tauri command) to spawn a real, visible terminal tab titled `Debug: <title>`, closable by the user through the terminal domain's own ordinary kill path, with no hidden second spawn surface (locked by the new `validateDebugRunInTerminalBoundary` AST contract). Proven end to end against a real spawned Python mock adapter that itself issues a real runInTerminal reverse request: the adapter's own received reply carries a real positive processId, a real terminal session is created and produces real PTY output, and the frontend notification's session id matches. As disclosed in platformGaps, this was never actually triggered by either of this feature's two real reference adapters (debugpy defaults to internalConsole; no lldb-dap launch configuration was constructed that requests it) -- only by a synthetic mock adapter built for this purpose -- and a real-adapter-triggered desktop exercise of this path is registered as part of E2E-010, not yet executed.

acceptanceResults.acceptance: Missing or untrusted adapters fail with actionable confirmation
acceptanceResults.result: Every adapter spawn/connect path is structurally gated trust-then-confirmation-then-action, locked by AST contracts (validateDebugAdapterSpawnBoundary, validateDebugAdapterConnectBoundary, validateDebugAdapterConfirmationBoundary, validateDebugTcpCompanionSpawnBoundary): trust.require_trusted must run first, then confirmation.require_confirmed keyed on the exact (command, args, transport) triple (not the workspace or the launch.json `type` string, so a silently swapped binary always re-prompts), with real positive/negative canary tests (a file-creation canary for stdio, a non-blocking TCP-accept-backlog canary for TCP) proving the gate is not merely cosmetic. Missing/malformed adapter configuration (`.plain/debug-adapters.json`/`.vscode/launch.json`) resolves deterministically to an actionable `adapter-not-found` error rather than silently doing nothing, covered by 20+ adversarial parser fixtures. S3 added a real trust-declined/empty-workspace UX (`plain-debug-trust.ts`, mirroring the terminal domain's own four-state flow) that this feature had not originally planned but discovered was a real UX gap during implementation -- without it, an untrusted workspace's `Plain: Start Debugging` only threw a raw WORKSPACE_NOT_TRUSTED error with no way to grant trust from that entry point.

results: pnpm check passed in full on 2026-07-29 (exit code 0, captured via redirection plus an explicit `echo EXIT=$?` rather than through a pipe): cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings both zero-diff/zero-warning; cargo test 1177/1177 (unchanged since F100 -- this feature's seven implementation slices plus this closeout touched zero Rust source); pnpm exec vitest run 77 test files, 1654 cases; node scripts/plain/check-boundaries.mjs 88 app sources / 145 Rust sources / 17 pinned runtime dependencies; node scripts/plain/check-bundle.mjs 1985 sources, 53 tracked transitional debt sources.

This feature's own tracked-debt trajectory, verified slice by slice against a real bundle rather than assumed: the F010-F100 baseline this feature inherited was 203 sources across five categories (chatAgent 121, mcp 16, authAccount 11, syncEditSessions 8, extensionRuntime 47), but acceptance 5 ('Language environments, remote, notebook, tasks and testing are removed') had zero coverage in that baseline. S0 (this feature's own frozen research document, finding 6, and the main session's own ruling point 4) found 57 more sources that had been in the bundle since F010 and in no baseline at all: one chatAgent file misclassified by a remote-sounding filename (remoteCodingAgentsService.js, 121 -> 122) and seven newly-tracked categories (notebook 23, tasks 1, testing 9, remote 11, languagePacks 2, languageDetection 2, treeSitter 8). Rather than reduce 203 while those 57 sat uncounted -- which would have flattered the metric without moving it -- S0 raised the honest baseline to 260 first, verified by a real pnpm build:frontend and check-bundle.mjs --print matching commit f87cc64e's own real numbers exactly. From that honest 260: S2 removed the mcp/syncEditSessions/authAccount (minus globalCompositeBar.js) stubs, 260 -> 231; S3 removed the chatAgent stubs (122 -> 9, the largest single removal), 231 -> 117; S4 migrated globalCompositeBar.js into app/ and closed authAccount's remaining tail, 117 -> 113; S5 severed extensionRuntime's only bundle-reachability path, 113 -> 84; S6 closed the seven newly-tracked categories from S0, 84 -> 53. sourceCount moved in step across the same slices: 2208 -> 2179 -> 2057 -> 2053 -> 2016 -> 1985, unchanged since. Every one of these numbers is a real, independently reproduced check-bundle.mjs count taken at the time of its own slice, not a retrospective estimate.

The final, honestly measured floor per category (docs/bundle-baseline.json's categoryNotes carries the full per-file dependency-graph audit; this is the summary): mcp 0, syncEditSessions 0, tasks 0, testing 0 -- all four real, verified zeros. authAccount 1 (authentication.service.js, kept alive by chatEntitlementService.js -- itself one of chatAgent's own 9 floor files -- injecting IAuthenticationService into a class this feature's own real dependency audit confirmed is never actually DI-constructed anywhere in the running app). languagePacks 1 (localizedStrings.js, kept alive by VS Code's own built-in browser-automation driver.js, unrelated to this project's own Tauri/Playwright harness). remote 4 (remoteAgentService.service.js pinned by IPathService/ILabelService, two foundational always-constructed services; remoteHosts.js pinned by four ordinary URI-parsing consumers unrelated to remote development; remoteAuthorityResolver.js/.service.js pinned by WebviewElement's own non-optional constructor parameter, reinstated after a real before/after rebuild proved removing it bought zero file-count benefit while adding real risk). chatAgent 9 (kept alive by the Command Palette, Go to Anything, Go to Symbol and Format Document -- ordinary, always-running Workbench features, not chat functionality). notebook 9 (kept alive by a customEditorInputFactory.js type-check import chain that never actually constructs a NotebookEditorInput, plus INotebookDocumentService's real, load-bearing use inside every file/Explorer label widget). extensionRuntime 19 (every one of the 11 extensions-service-override package files is gone entirely; the 19 that remain back Format Document, Format Document With..., Change Language Mode and the declarative ExtensionsRegistry configuration/theme/snippet contribution mechanism AGENTS.md itself sanctions). languageDetection 2 and treeSitter 8 (both deliberately untouched -- see the S6 zero-benefit findings below).

S5 is this project's fourth documented case of pnpm check passing completely while a real user-facing path was broken, and the first of the four with a genuinely new failure shape. The first version of the patch correctly deleted missing-services.js's global registerSingleton(IExtensionService, NullExtensionService, InstantiationType.Eager) and correctly added app/services.ts's own binding of IExtensionService to PlainNullExtensionService inside initialize()'s services map -- types checked, the AST contract passed, all 17 of PlainNullExtensionService's own unit tests passed, cargo test and the bundle ratchet were untouched and green. Full pnpm test:e2e:browser then failed 97 of 98 scenarios, all with the identical <body data-plain-ready='error'> bootstrap failure. Running a single scenario directly surfaced the real error: '[createInstance] hoverService depends on extensionService which is NOT registered.' The root cause was not a missing registration but the same token bound through two non-equivalent mechanisms: consumers resolved through the global singleton registry (which the patch had just emptied of this token) are constructed before initialize()'s services map ever takes effect, so binding IExtensionService only in the services map left every early global-registry consumer -- hoverService among them -- looking at an empty slot. The fix was for app/services.ts to also call registerSingleton(IExtensionService, PlainNullExtensionService, InstantiationType.Eager) directly, restoring the mechanism the patch had removed rather than replacing it with a different one. None of pnpm check's own steps could have caught this: the SyncDescriptor's type was correct, the AST contract checks shape rather than timing, and the unit tests construct an isolated object rather than a real container -- none of those three layers ever runs a real bootstrap. This is the same failure class as three earlier incidents in this project (F090 S0's zero-width blame decorations that never rendered, F090 S1's history view with zero DI decorators that threw on click, F100 S3's onMouseDown deleting a breakpoint before its own context menu could fire) -- every one only visible at real runtime/DOM timing, which is exactly why this feature's own discipline treats a full pnpm test:e2e:browser pass, not a green pnpm check, as the actual delivery bar.

S6 made two deliberate zero-touch decisions after real dependency-graph audits, not oversights. languageDetection's ILanguageDetectionService is resolved unconditionally at the top of editorStatus.js's real, always-registered Change Language Mode command (Ctrl+K Ctrl+M, f1: true) before any other logic runs, the same load-bearing pattern S5 already found for IExtensionGalleryService -- removing it would reproduce S5's own bootstrap-death class on a real, everyday command instead of at boot. treeSitter's ITreeSitterLibraryService has a second, entirely independent registerSingleton inside standaloneServices.js (unconditionally loaded by base-service-override) with the identical always-false supportsLanguage() behavior as the missing-services.js stub this slice would have removed -- deleting the missing-services.js copy would have been genuinely zero-benefit, confirmed by real content inspection that both registrations behave identically. Both categories were left at their S0-frozen values (2 and 8) by deliberate choice, documented before any patch edit was attempted. S6 also removed and then reverted IRemoteAuthorityResolverService after a real before/after rebuild showed removing it changed the remote category's file count not at all (webviewElement.js's own non-optional constructor dependency on it, independent of missing-services.js, kept the file reachable regardless) while adding real risk with no equivalent fallback registration to lean on -- reverted via git stash rather than shipped as a speculative improvement. Separately, S6 flagged, and this closeout repeats rather than resolves, a genuine unexplained anomaly: workbench/api/common/extHostTypes/notebooks.js was already reachable in the bundle before this feature ever touched anything, and an exhaustive grep across the entire installed dependency tree (every @codingame/* package, every nested .pnpm store copy, app/ itself) found zero real importers of it or of the file that re-exports from it. Its presence is inert regardless of the mechanism keeping it in the source map, but why it is reachable at all remains genuinely unknown and is recorded as an open question for a future slice, not smoothed over as explained.

The runtime excluded-surface guard (app/excluded-surface-policy.ts's findExcludedWorkbenchSurfaces, enforced by app/excluded-surfaces.ts's enforceExcludedWorkbenchSurfaces at bootstrap) changes role with this feature's completion, and this closeout verified rather than assumed the change is safe by reading the guard's own implementation: it is a pure blacklist that captures whatever command/view/contribution ids are actually registered at the time it runs and matches them against six category regexes, throwing only if the intersection is non-empty -- it asserts nothing about any id's existence and cannot fail merely because a target disappeared. Before this feature, it was the only line of defense proving the excluded chat/agent/mcp/auth/sync/notebook/task/testing/remote surfaces were unreachable, because the underlying bundle debt (203, later found to be 260) still physically existed. After this feature's real removals, for the four categories that reached a true zero (mcp, syncEditSessions, tasks, testing) there is no longer any registerable id these regexes could even match in the first place -- the guard becomes redundant for those categories rather than load-bearing, which is already demonstrated empirically rather than only by code reading: PLAIN_EXCLUDED_SURFACE_GUARD_V1 was never once thrown across any of this feature's Browser E2E runs. For the categories that remain at a non-zero floor (authAccount, chatAgent, extensionRuntime, notebook, remote, languagePacks, languageDetection, treeSitter), the guard keeps its original, load-bearing role, since those floor files are real, reachable vendor code and the guard is what proves none of it registers a user-facing id a user could actually reach. The guard was deliberately kept for the zeroed categories too, as defense in depth against a future regression reintroducing a matching id through a path this feature's own bundle analysis does not cover, at zero known cost.

This closeout also found and fixed a stale, self-contradictory guard in scripts/plain/check-bundle.mjs, discovered while preparing to flip F110 to complete. A check written on this project's very first day (2026-07-18, commit 3fe6c358f, long before F110 was researched) asserted that once features.json marked F110 complete, no bundle source path could end with /missing-services.js. A real pnpm build:frontend run during this closeout confirmed missing-services.js is still present in the real dist source map today, and necessarily remains present under the architecture the main session actually ruled on (decision point 1: patch surgery, not a services.js facade rewrite) -- that file still legitimately registers roughly 80 non-debt service stubs (IHoverService, IUndoRedoService, IUriIdentityService, IKeyboardLayoutService among them) this feature was never in scope to remove. The stale check would have made marking F110 complete fail pnpm check permanently, for a file whose continued presence is the intended, accepted final state rather than a residual. It has been removed, with an explanatory comment recording why and what it assumed, in favor of the check that was already running unconditionally on every pnpm check and is the strictly correct proof: the token-level content scan (forbiddenDebtTokenStrings) that greps the entire built dist/**/*.js for every specific token string this feature's own patches removed from missing-services.js/services.js, regardless of feature status. This is disclosed here in full rather than folded silently into the closeout: it is a change to guard/script code (scripts/plain/check-bundle.mjs, not app/ or src-tauri/ product code), narrow, precedented by every one of S0-S6's own routine guard/contract-script edits, and it does not weaken any actual security guarantee since the more precise token-level scan it defers to was already in force.

S5 (entitlements): created src-tauri/Entitlements.plist containing only com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit=true. A real plutil -lint pass first showed the file well-formed, but a real ad-hoc-signed pnpm tauri:build:e2e (with APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY=- to force real, non-default codesigning) then failed with 'Failed to parse entitlements: AMFIUnserializeXML: syntax error near line 13' -- Apple's own entitlements parser (AMFI) is stricter than the general CoreFoundation plist parser plutil uses and rejects a literal '--' sequence inside an XML comment, a real XML-spec rule most tooling tolerates but AMFI does not; this project's own prose style uses '--' as an em dash throughout, so the file's original explanatory comment tripped it. Fixed by keeping Entitlements.plist itself comment-free and moving the rationale into scripts/plain/boundary-contracts.mjs's own EXPECTED_ENTITLEMENTS comment instead. After the fix, a real ad-hoc-signed build (APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY=-) produced a Plain.app with CodeDirectory flags=0x10002(adhoc,runtime) (hardened runtime genuinely on) and codesign -d --entitlements - showing com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit=true embedded; the raw signed binary was launched directly (not via a GUI Computer Use session) and stayed running for 4 seconds with no crash and no error output, the specific failure mode the research document's own '结论 4.3' warned hardened-runtime-without-JIT-entitlement causes. Separately discovered and disclosed rather than silently worked around: Tauri's bundler only invokes codesign (and therefore only ever applies bundle.macOS.entitlements) when some signingIdentity is actually configured -- the project's real default build path (no identity configured, matching the currently-accepted ad-hoc-only decision) does not touch codesign/entitlements at all and produces the same bare linker-applied ad-hoc signature as before this feature (confirmed: reverted the one-off APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY=- test after verifying it, and a fresh default pnpm tauri:build:e2e reproduced the pre-existing flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed), zero-entitlements state exactly). signingIdentity was deliberately NOT added as a permanent tauri.conf.json default: doing so would have made every local build on this development machine specifically start failing at the DMG/entitlements-adjacent xattr step (see the CI note below) due to an unrelated, pre-existing Anaconda-installed xattr shadowing the real macOS /usr/bin/xattr on this machine's PATH -- a real, reproduced local-environment quirk, disclosed here rather than fixed by silently rewriting build scripts and their locked-string contracts for a machine-specific problem outside this task's scope.

S5 (the com.apple.security.cs.debugger question): ran a real, bounded, reproducible experiment rather than deciding from documentation alone. A small C harness (posix_spawn a child, then task_for_pid(mach_task_self(), childPid, ...)) was compiled and ad-hoc codesigned two ways. Without any entitlement: task_for_pid fails fast and cleanly (KERN_FAILURE, no hang) -- reproduced twice. Re-signed with only com.apple.security.cs.debugger added: the identical call reliably blocks and had to be force-killed -- reproduced twice, with the process tree confirmed stuck via ps (not merely a timeout). Real Apple lldb itself (already signed by Apple with whatever entitlements it needs) was also run directly (lldb -o 'process launch' -o quit -- <target>) in this same environment and hung identically at process launch, reproducing F100's own original finding in a fresh session. DevToolsSecurity -status reports Developer Mode disabled on this machine with no passwordless path to enable it (enabling it would itself be a system security setting change, correctly out of bounds regardless of task convenience). Together: the entitlement measurably changes kernel-level behavior for the immediate caller regardless of what spawned it (consistent with the research document's 结论 4.4 caller-based correction -- Plain.app spawning an adapter is not the same as Plain.app being the caller of task_for_pid), but this specific sandboxed execution environment cannot complete real native process debugging at all, for reasons independent of any entitlement Plain.app itself carries.
